cases.situation: Going to a fintech conference alone next week and I freeze up at the coffee breaks. Give me something to say to someone standing by the coffee.
cases.reply: Hi, I'm Sam. Which session brought you here? I came for the fraud panel and half of it went over my head.
cases.note: One question plus one line about you. The next question comes from their answer: 'What's the part people don't get about that?'

cases.situation: 每周一在电梯里都会碰到隔壁部门的李姐，我只知道她上个月去新疆玩了。每次都尴尬地各自看手机。
cases.reply: 李姐早！上个月去新疆，哪一站最值得去？
cases.note: 记得对方说过的事最管用；接下来的问题从她的回答里找，别换话题。

cases.situation: At my girlfriend's work party, chatting with a guy named Chris who's given me one-word answers twice now. How do I get out without it being awkward?
cases.reply: I'm going to grab another drink. Good to meet you, Chris, enjoy the rest of the night.
cases.note: Two flat answers is the cue. Exit warmly and don't make it a verdict on either of you.

cases.situation: Meeting my boyfriend Arjun's dad for the first time at dinner on Saturday. Arjun says he's quiet and spends weekends restoring old Royal Enfield motorbikes in the garage. I want something to say that isn't about work.
cases.reply: Arjun tells me you restore old Royal Enfields. Which one's in the garage at the moment?
cases.note: Open on the thing he cares about, then let the next question come from his answer ("How long does one take, start to finish?") and share one small thing back before returning to him.

cases.situation: First video call with my new team and I'm always early. It'll probably be just me and Inês, who's based in Lisbon, waiting for a few minutes. All I know is she's the data analyst.
cases.reply: Hi Inês, looks like we're the early ones. I'm new this week, so I'll just ask: what's one thing about this team you wish someone had told you in your first month?
cases.note: Asks for a view she actually has, which gives a thread to follow; the next question should come from her answer.
